Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Over the past few days I’ve noticed swelling around my eyes and also in my ankles, and I feel more fatigued than usual. I was recently diagnosed with Hodgkin’s lymphoma but haven’t started treatment yet, and I haven’t noticed any changes in my urine.

“No, I haven’t had spinning vertigo or dizziness when I change head position or roll over in bed.”

“No, I haven’t had any sudden chest pain, and I haven’t experienced sudden episodes that feel like heart failure. The main issues have been the swelling around my eyes and ankles and feeling more fatigued.”

“No, I haven’t had unintentional weight loss, night sweats, or recurrent fevers. It’s mainly the swelling around my eyes and ankles and the increased fatigue.”

“No, I haven’t noticed bright red blood in my stool, and I don’t have any pain or itching around hemorrhoids. The swelling around my eyes and ankles and my fatigue are what I’ve been focused on.”

“No, I haven’t had any involuntary muscle weakness that improves after brief exercise. I’m mainly noticing swelling around my eyes and ankles and feeling more fatigued than usual.”
